card.name: Opening words of evidence-limit statements
card.fires_on: Small words at the start of a sentence that states limits of the evidence, such as "There <<are>>" before "no adequate studies", "Based <<on>>" available data, or "The <<findings>>" of increased risk. Seen in warnings and pregnancy sections.

modes.label: There are no adequate studies
modes.description: The word "are" (or a comma) after "There" just before a statement that no adequate, well-controlled studies exist.
modes.example: There<< are>> no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant

modes.label: Findings of increased risk
modes.description: The noun "finding" or "findings" at the start of a sentence about whether observed increased mortality or risk applies more widely.
modes.example: The extent to which the<< findings>> of increased mortality in observational studies may be

modes.label: Based on available data
modes.description: The word "on" after a sentence-opening "Based" before a hedged conclusion.
